mainTopic: A woman who bleeds from תשמיש and how she is tested, stories of cures, and when a woman must count שבעה נקיים (רבי's decree, the women's stringency, a miscarriage, a new כלה)
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about a woman who bleeds every time she has תשמיש. After three times with her first or second husband she must get divorced and may remarry. After three times with her third husband she must do a בדיקה with a lead tube to see whether the blood comes from the מקור (impure) or from the sides (pure). A wound or a fixed וסת can also explain the blood, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and the Sages argue whether wound blood from the מקור is טמא. ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן discuss why the test is delayed. Then come stories of women brought to רבי, שמואל and רבי יוחנן for cures. Next, the גמרא turns to counting days: רבי's decree for the outlying fields, and רבי זירא's report that Jewish women count שבעה נקיים for even a mustard-seed drop of blood. רבא rules on a miscarriage after two days of labor and says that a woman who accepts a marriage proposal must count שבעה נקיים, which רבינא applies even to a young bride. A new teaching of רבא about a woman begins at the end and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: After the first husband: she may marry someone else
steps.stepSummary: The end of the ruling about the first husband: after three times she must get divorced, and she is allowed to marry another man.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...and she may marry another man.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is finishing a sentence that started just before this section. A woman who bled because of תשמיש with her first husband three times must get divorced, and here it says she may then marry another man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the bleeding may be connected to this particular husband. So she is not banned from marriage altogether. She may try again with a different man.

phrases.english: and she may marry another man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ruling about the first husband, which started before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After three times with the first husband she must get divorced, and she may marry someone else.

steps.title: With the second husband: the same three-time limit applies
steps.stepSummary: If she bleeds because of תשמיש with her second husband, she again has three times. After that she must get divorced and may marry a third man.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she married another man and saw blood because of תשמיש, she may have תשמיש a first, second, and third time. From then on she may not have תשמיש until she gets divorced and marries another man.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא repeats the same rule for the second husband. Three times are allowed, then divorce, and then she may marry a third man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after it happened with one husband, a second husband gets a fresh start. The problem may still be connected to the man, so she gets another chance with someone new.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'first, second, third' as three different husbands. Inside each marriage, she gets three times with that husband.

phrases.english: If she married another man,
and saw blood because of marital relations —
she may have relations a first time,
and a second and a third time;
from here on she may not have relations
until she is divorced and marries another man.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִיסֵּת לְאַחֵר, וְרָאֲתָה דָּם מֵחֲמַת תַּשְׁמִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same three-time rule to the second husband.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With the second husband she also gets three times, then must get divorced, and may marry a third man.

steps.title: With the third husband: she must now examine herself
steps.stepSummary: If it happens again with the third husband, after three times she may not continue until she does a בדיקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she married another man and saw blood because of תשמיש, she may have תשמיש a first, second, and third time. From then on she may not have תשמיש until she examines herself.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא reaches the third husband. The ending changes: instead of 'until she gets divorced,' it now says 'until she examines herself.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: After it has happened with three different men, we can no longer say the husband is the cause. The problem seems to be her own, so changing husbands will not help. Only a בדיקה can show whether the blood is the impure kind.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the turning point of the ברייתא. The answer is no longer 'try a different husband' but 'find out where the blood comes from.' That leads straight into the method of בדיקה.

phrases.english: If she married another man,
and saw blood because of marital relations —
she may have relations a first time,
and a second and a third time;
from here on she may not have relations
until she examines herself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same structure as step 2, but the ending changes from divorce to בדיקה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After three times with the third husband, she may not continue until she does a בדיקה.

steps.title: How is the examination done?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how she examines herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does she examine herself?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The ברייתא asks a practical question to introduce the method of בדיקה that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 required a בדיקה but did not explain what it is. This question opens the explanation.

phrases.english: How does she examine herself?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the details of the בדיקה required in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical method of the self-examination.

steps.title: The tube test and how to read the result
steps.stepSummary: She uses a tube with a brush inside and a cloth on its tip. Blood on the tip means it came from the מקור. No blood on the tip means it came from the sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: She brings a tube with a brush inside it and a cloth placed on the brush's tip. If blood is found on the tip of the cloth, it is clear that it came from the מקור. If no blood is found on the tip, it is clear that it came from the sides.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא describes the tool for the בדיקה and explains how to read the result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only blood from the מקור (the uterus) makes her impure. Blood from the sides (the walls) does not. The tube lets the cloth reach deep inside, so blood on its tip points to the מקור. A clean tip shows the blood came from the sides, so she is pure and may continue.

keyTerms.meaning: the source (the uterus); blood from here makes her impure
the sides (walls); blood from here does not make her impure

steps.whatToRemember: The key question is where the blood comes from. מקור means impure, צדדין means pure, and the tube test is how she tells the difference.

phrases.english: She brings a tube,
and inside it a brush,
and a cloth placed on its tip.

phrases.aramaic: אִם נִמְצָא דָּם עַל רֹאשׁ הַמּוֹךְ —
phrases.english: If blood is found on the tip of the cloth —
it is clear that it comes from the source (uterus).
If blood is not found on its tip —
it is clear that it comes from the sides.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A tube with a brush and a cloth on its tip. Blood on the tip means מקור (impure). No blood on the tip means sides (pure).

steps.title: Blaming the blood on a wound or on a fixed cycle
steps.stepSummary: If she has a wound in that place, she may blame the blood on the wound. If she has a fixed וסת, she may blame the blood on her וסת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if she has a wound in that place, she attributes the blood to her wound. And if she has a fixed cycle, she attributes the blood to her cycle.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds two cases where she may explain the blood by something other than תשמיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wound there gives a likely source of blood that is not from the מקור, so she is pure. A fixed וסת means the bleeding is tied to her regular cycle and not to תשמיש. So at other times she is not assumed to bleed because of תשמיש.

keyTerms.meaning: she attributes / blames (the blood on something)

steps.whatToRemember: Even a woman who keeps bleeding at תשמיש is not automatically forbidden. A wound or a fixed וסת can explain the blood.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם יֵשׁ לָהּ מַכָּה בְּאוֹתוֹ מָקוֹם —
phrases.english: And if she has a wound in that place —
she attributes it to her wound;
and if she has a fixed cycle —
she attributes it to her cycle.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם יֵשׁ לָהּ מַכָּה בְּאוֹתוֹ מָקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds cases where the restriction does not apply because the blood has another explanation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wound or a fixed וסת allows her to blame the blood on that cause instead of on תשמיש.

steps.title: Wound blood must match, and she is believed about a wound
steps.stepSummary: If her wound's blood looks different from the blood she sees, she cannot blame it on the wound. A woman is believed to say she has a wound in the מקור. These are the words of רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the blood from her wound looks different from the blood she sees, she cannot blame it on the wound. A woman is believed when she says, 'I have a wound in the מקור that bleeds.' This is רבי's opinion.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a limit to the rule from step 6 about blaming blood on a wound. It also says a woman is trusted to report that she has a wound.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 allowed her to blame the blood on a wound. Now we learn this works only if the blood looks the same as the wound's blood. Different-looking blood shows it did not come from the wound. רבי also trusts her own word that a wound exists inside the מקור, even though no one can see it.

keyTerms.meaning: Blames, attributes (the blood to a cause)
The uterus, where real נדה blood comes from

phrases.english: And if the blood of her wound
was different from the blood she sees
she may not blame it on the wound,
and a woman is believed to say,
"I have a wound in the uterus
from which blood comes out,"
these are the words of Rabbi.
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה הנשיא.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם הָיָה דַּם מַכָּתָהּ מְשׁוּנֶּה מִדַּם רְאִיָּיתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to step 6's permission to blame the blood on a wound
steps.mimraCoreRuling: She may blame the blood on a wound only if the blood matches the wound's blood. She is believed about having a wound in the מקור (רבי).

steps.title: Is wound blood from the uterus impure or pure
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says wound blood coming from the מקור is טמא. A testimony of our Sages says it is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: blood from a wound that comes out of the מקור is impure. But our Rabbis testified that wound blood coming from the מקור is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings two views that disagree. One says wound blood from the מקור is טמא, and the other says it is טהור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we assumed wound blood is not נדה blood. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees and holds that wound blood is still טמא if it comes from the מקור. The Sages' testimony says it stays טהור, because it is only a wound.

keyTerms.meaning: They testified, passing on a received tradition

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two views. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says טמא. The Sages' testimony says טהור.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Blood of a wound that comes from the uterus
is impure,
but our Rabbis testified

phrases.aramaic: עַל דַּם הַמַּכָּה הַבָּא מִן הַמָּקוֹר
phrases.english: about the blood of a wound that comes from the uterus
that it is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a disagreement about the status of wound blood from the מקור
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: wound blood from the מקור is טמא. The Sages' testimony: it is טהור.

steps.title: What is the difference between them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the two views in step 8 really argue about.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the disagreement in step 8. This sets up עולא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both views agree the blood comes from a wound, so it is not real נדה blood. The question is what makes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל call it טמא anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 8's disagreement
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying point on which רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and the Sages' testimony disagree

steps.title: They argue whether the uterus itself makes blood impure
steps.stepSummary: עולא says they argue over whether the place of the מקור is itself טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: the difference between them is whether the place of the מקור is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא explains the disagreement. It depends on whether passing through the מקור makes any blood טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that the מקור itself is a טמא place. So any blood coming out of it becomes טמא, even wound blood. The Sages hold that only blood that truly begins as נדה blood is טמא, so wound blood stays טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: The place of the uterus is itself impure
There is a difference between them

steps.whatToRemember: The argument is whether the מקור makes blood טמא just because the blood came out of there (רבן שמעון בן גמליאל), or only real נדה blood is טמא (the Sages).

phrases.english: Ulla said:
whether the place of the uterus is impure
phrases.notes: He means: does any blood that passes through there become impure, even wound blood?

phrases.english: is the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא מָקוֹר מְקוֹמוֹ טָמֵא אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They argue whether the מקור itself is a טמא place that makes any blood leaving it טמא

steps.title: Won't the tube scratch her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the tube בדיקה from step 5. The tube could scratch her and cause bleeding, which would ruin the test.
steps.simpleTranslation: A tube? It will scratch her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the tube used for the בדיקה in step 5. It objects that the tube itself might cause a wound.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test only works if any blood found came from her body on its own. If the tube scratches her, the blood could come from the scratch, and the בדיקה would prove nothing.

phrases.english: A tube?
It will surely scratch her!
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets. The words in square brackets are the corrected wording, and both mean roughly the same thing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the טמא/טהור argument and goes back to the tube from step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: The tube בדיקה described in step 5
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The tube may scratch her and cause bleeding, so any blood found would not prove where her bleeding comes from

steps.title: A smooth lead tube with a folded-in edge
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that the tube is made of soft lead and its opening is folded inward, so it does not scratch.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: it is a tube made of lead, and its opening is folded inward.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the challenge in step 11. He describes a tube built so that it cannot scratch her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lead is soft, and the folded-in edge leaves no sharp rim. So the tube does not cause any wound, and the בדיקה from step 5 stays reliable.
steps.whatToRemember: The בדיקה tube is made of lead with a folded-in edge, so it cannot cause bleeding that would spoil the test.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
It is with a tube of lead,
and its mouth is folded inward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the case more precisely (what the tube is made of and how it is shaped)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any tube might scratch her and make the test useless
steps.terutzMaskana: A soft lead tube with a folded-in opening does not scratch, so the בדיקה works

steps.title: Why not test her already with the first husband?
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש asks why the woman must be divorced at all. She could do the בדיקה after the third time with her first husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said to רבי יוחנן: Let her examine herself after the third time with her first husband!
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש challenges the order of the process. Why wait for a second and third husband before doing the tube בדיקה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule says she is divorced after bleeding three times with one husband, and only later, with the third husband, does she test herself. ריש לקיש asks: if the test can tell us where the blood comes from, use it right away and save the marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: An examination, here done with the tube, to find where the blood comes from

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said to Rabbi Yochanan:
But let her examine herself at the third act of relations
phrases.notes: He means with the tube test from step 5.

phrases.english: with the first husband?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וְתִבְדּוֹק עַצְמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how the tube works (steps 11-12) to when the test should be done.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that she is tested only after three husbands
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the test works, using it with the first husband would avoid a needless divorce.

steps.title: Not all husbands are the same
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that a different husband might not cause bleeding, so it is better not to test yet.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Because not all fingers are equal.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains why we do not test her with the first husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bleeding might come from this particular husband. With another man she might not bleed at all. A test might show the blood comes from the מקור and make her forbidden to everyone, so it is better to let her remarry first and see.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'fingers'; a polite way of referring to the men's bodies

steps.confusionAlert: 'Fingers' here is not about the woman's examination with a finger. It is a polite word for the husbands' bodies, which differ from one man to another.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין כׇּל הָאֶצְבָּעוֹת שָׁווֹת.
phrases.english: He said to him: Because not all fingers are equal.
phrases.notes: A polite way of saying not every man's body is the same, so the next husband may not cause bleeding.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Testing early would save the first marriage.
steps.terutzMaskana: Bleeding may depend on the husband, so remarriage might solve it without risking a test.

steps.title: Why not test after the first time with the third husband?
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש asks why she waits three times with the third husband, instead of testing after the first time.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Let her examine herself after the first time with the third husband!
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש asks a second timing question, this time about the third husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the third husband she has already bled with two different men, so the pattern seems clear. Why not test right away after the first time with him?

phrases.english: He said to him: But let her examine herself
at the first act of relations with the third husband?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְתִבְדּוֹק עַצְמָהּ בְּבִיאָה רִאשׁוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge on the same timing rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: Waiting three times with the third husband before testing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: After two husbands the pattern seems proven, so one time with the third should be enough.

steps.title: One time is not enough to show a pattern
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the strength of relations differs from time to time, so one bleeding may be a fluke.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because not all forces are equal.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers why she must wait three times even with the third husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A single bleeding could come from how forceful that particular act was. Only after three times is it clear that this husband regularly causes bleeding, and only then is the test needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Forces, meaning how forceful a particular act of relations was

steps.whatToRemember: Two reasons to delay the test: husbands differ (step 14), and each time differs (step 16). We test only once a real pattern is set.

phrases.english: Because not all forces are equal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One bleeding with the third husband already proves the pattern.
steps.terutzMaskana: One time could be a fluke, so three times are needed.

steps.title: רבי cures a woman by frightening her
steps.stepSummary: A bleeding woman came to רבי. He had אבדן frighten her, a blood clot fell out, and רבי said she was cured.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain woman came before רבי. He told אבדן: Go frighten her. He went and frightened her, and a clot of blood fell from her. רבי said: This woman is cured.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a practical way to cure a woman who bleeds from relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sudden fright pushed out a clot of blood that was causing the bleeding. Once it came out, רבי ruled that the problem was gone.

phrases.english: A certain woman who came before Rabbi,
He said to Abdan: Go frighten her.
He went and frightened her,
and a clot of blood fell from her.
Rabbi said: This woman is cured.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the timing discussion, the גמרא brings a story about curing the bleeding.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If fright pushes out a blood clot, the woman is cured.

steps.title: שמואל tries the same method, but nothing comes out
steps.stepSummary: A woman came to שמואל. He had רב דימי בר יוסף frighten her, but nothing fell from her.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain woman came before שמואל. He told רב דימי בר יוסף: Go frighten her! He went and frightened her, but nothing at all fell from her.
steps.whatsHappening: A second story with the same method but a different result. It sets up שמואל's ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל used the same cure that רבי used. This time no clot came out, so the cure did not work here.

phrases.aramaic: הַהִיא אִתְּתָא דַּאֲתַאי לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּמָר שְׁמוּאֵל,
phrases.english: A certain woman who came before Mar Shmuel,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ לְרַב דִּימִי בַּר יוֹסֵף: זִיל בַּעֲתַהּ!
phrases.english: He said to Rav Dimi bar Yosef: Go frighten her!
He went and frightened her,
and nothing at all fell from her.
phrases.notes: Both bracketed words mean 'from her'; the corrected wording uses the Aramaic מינה instead of the Hebrew ממנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהִיא אִתְּתָא דַּאֲתַאי לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּמָר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same method as step 17, but with the opposite result.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Frightening her did not push anything out.

steps.title: שמואל: a woman who fills and empties has no cure
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that this woman's body keeps filling with blood and letting it out, and such a woman cannot be cured.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: This one fills up and shakes out, and any woman who fills up and shakes out has no remedy.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל explains why the cure failed and gives a general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With רבי's woman there was one clot causing the problem, and once it came out she was healed. Here the blood keeps building up and coming out again during relations. There is no single clot to remove, so there is no cure.

keyTerms.meaning: Fills up (with blood) and shakes it out

steps.whatToRemember: Fright can cure bleeding caused by a single clot (רבי's case). It cannot help a woman whose body keeps filling and emptying with blood (שמואל's case).

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: זוֹ מְמַלְּאָה וְנוֹפֶצֶת הִיא,
phrases.english: Shmuel said: This one fills up and shakes out,
phrases.notes: Her body keeps filling with blood and letting it out during relations.

phrases.english: and any woman who fills up and shakes out
has no remedy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: זוֹ מְמַלְּאָה וְנוֹפֶצֶת הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the failed result of step 18 and sets a general rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman who keeps filling with blood and letting it out has no cure.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The fright method works only when one clot is the cause of the bleeding.

steps.title: A woman who bleeds after every טבילה comes to רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: A woman sees blood every time she comes up from her טבילת מצוה. רבי יוחנן suggests the jealous talk of the town's women is causing it, and tells her to be with her husband by the river.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a woman who came to רבי יוחנן. Every time she came up from her מצוה immersion, she saw blood. He told her: Maybe the gossip of the women in your town has affected you. Go and be with your husband by the riverbank.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells another story about a woman with a bleeding problem, this time brought to רבי יוחנן. He gives her practical advice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her bleeding comes at exactly the wrong moment: right after the טבילה that should permit her to her husband. רבי יוחנן thinks the cause is the jealous talk (an evil eye) of the town's women. His fix is to go somewhere else, to the river, so they don't see her.

keyTerms.meaning: The required immersion that permits a woman to her husband
The whispering or gossip of your town
And be with him (your husband) as husband and wife
On the bank of the river

phrases.english: A certain woman who came before Rabbi Yochanan,
because every time she would come up
from the מצוה immersion,
phrases.notes: This is her required immersion in the מקוה that permits her to her husband.

phrases.english: she would see blood.
He said to her: Perhaps the gossip of your town
has come upon you,
go and be with him
on the bank of the river.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another story in the same series of women with bleeding problems brought to sages (רבי, שמואל, now רבי יוחנן).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן attributes her bleeding after טבילה to the town's jealous gossip and tells her to immerse and be with her husband by the river.

steps.title: Second version: tell your friends so they come over to your side
steps.stepSummary: Another version of רבי יוחנן's advice: she should tell her friends about her problem, so the women who were against her will become supportive.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say he told her: Tell your friends. That way, those who were against you on this side will be with you on that side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of what רבי יוחנן told the woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version she doesn't hide from the women. She openly tells them her trouble, so their jealousy turns into sympathy. The idea is the same as before (the women's attitude is the problem), but the cure is the opposite: openness instead of hiding.

phrases.english: Some say, he said to her:
Reveal it to your friends.
so that those who were against you on this side,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets, and some have the word in square brackets instead. The meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: will be with you on that side.
phrases.notes: Meaning they will switch from talking against her to being on her side.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמַר, אֲמַר לַהּ: תְּגַלִּי לְחַבְרוֹתִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative version of רבי יוחנן's advice from step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: She should tell her friends, so the women who were against her will turn to her side.

steps.title: Third version: tell your friends so they will pray for you
steps.stepSummary: A third version: she should tell her friends so they will pray for her. This is supported by a ברייתא saying a person in pain should tell the public so they pray for him, learned from the מצורע calling out 'טמא טמא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say he told her: Tell your friends, so they will pray for mercy for you. As a ברייתא teaches on the verse 'and he shall call out: Impure, impure': a person must let the public know his pain, and the public will pray for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third version of רבי יוחנן's advice and backs it up with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the reason for telling her friends is not to win them over but to get their prayers. The ברייתא learns from the מצורע, who calls out 'טמא טמא', that a suffering person should make his pain known so many people will pray for him.

keyTerms.meaning: They will ask for mercy (pray) for you
And he shall call out: Impure, impure (said about the מְצֹרָע)
To make his pain known to the public

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא teaches a lasting lesson: sharing one's trouble with others is a way to bring on their prayers, and it is not something to be ashamed of.

phrases.english: And some say, he said to her:
Reveal it to your friends,
so that they will ask for mercy for you,
as it is taught: "And he shall call out: Impure, impure" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:45, about the מצורע.

phrases.english: he must make his pain known to the public,
and the public will ask for mercy on him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמַר, אֲמַר לָהּ: גַּלִּי לְחַבְרוֹתִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third version of רבי יוחנן's advice. Same action as step 21 (tell her friends), but for a different reason (prayer), and supported by a ברייתא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא on ויקרא 13:45: the מצורע announces his pain so the public will pray for him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: She should tell her friends so they will pray for her, just as a suffering person should let the public know so they pray for him.

steps.title: רב יוסף: a similar case in פומבדיתא, and she was healed
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף reports that a case like this happened in פומבדיתא, the advice was followed, and the woman was healed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: There was such a case in פומבדיתא, and she was healed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף adds a real-life report showing that this kind of advice worked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This short line confirms from experience that a woman with this problem was cured. It closes the story of the woman who bled after her טבילה.

keyTerms.meaning: An actual incident, a case that happened
פומבדיתא, a major Torah town in Bavel

steps.whatToRemember: A woman who bled after every טבילה was told by רבי יוחנן either to go to the river or to tell her friends (so they would support her or pray for her). רב יוסף confirms such a woman was healed.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: הֲוָה עוֹבָדָא בְּפוּמְבְּדִיתָא,
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: There was an incident in Pumbedita,
and she was healed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: הֲוָה עוֹבָדָא בְּפוּמְבְּדִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms from a real case that the advice in steps 20-22 worked.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a similar case in פומבדיתא, the woman was healed.

steps.title: רבי's decree for the outlying fields: one day of blood means six more days
steps.stepSummary: A new topic begins. רב quotes a decree of רבי: in the outlying fields, a woman who saw blood on one day must sit six days plus that day. The statement continues past this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said in the name of רב יהודה, who said in the name of רב: רבי decreed in the fields: if she saw blood one day, she must sit six days and that day...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: a stricter rule רבי set up for women living in outlying areas. The statement is just starting here, and step 25 finishes it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By basic law, a woman who sees one day of blood during her days of זיבה may only need to wait one day. But in the fields, where people did not know how to tell נדה days from זיבה days, רבי made a stricter rule. She counts six clean days plus the day she saw.

keyTerms.meaning: Made a decree, set up a rule
In the fields, the outlying areas far from Torah scholars
She must sit (count) six days and that day

steps.confusionAlert: This is a new topic, not part of the stories about women who were cured. Here the subject is a rabbinic decree about how many days to count.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said that Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Rabbi decreed in the fields,
phrases.notes: The fields are faraway places where people didn't know these laws well.

phrases.english: if she saw blood one day —
she must sit six days and that day,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic, moving from stories about healing to a rabbinic decree about counting days.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי decreed that in the outlying fields, a woman who sees blood one day must count six days plus that day (the rule continues in step 25).

steps.title: רבי's decree continued: two days or three days of bleeding
steps.stepSummary: The decree of רבי continues. A woman who saw blood two days waits six more days plus those two. A woman who saw blood three days counts שבעה נקיים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she saw blood for two days, she sits six days plus those two. If she saw blood for three days, she sits seven clean days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting רבי's decree for the outlying fields. It explains what a woman does if she saw blood for two days or for three days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because people in the fields did not keep careful track of their days, רבי made them wait for every possibility. With two days of blood, the second day might be the start of her נדה period, so she waits until seven days have passed from it. With three days of blood, she might be a זבה גדולה, so she needs seven fully clean days.

keyTerms.meaning: Seven clean days, with no blood seen, counted before immersing
A woman who saw blood three days in a row outside her normal time; she must count seven clean days
A woman in her regular monthly period, who waits seven days from when it starts

steps.whatToRemember: In רבי's decree, the waiting period grows with the number of days she bled: one day leads to seven total, two days leads to eight total, and three days leads to seven clean days.

phrases.english: If she saw blood two days, she sits six, plus those two days
If three days, she sits seven clean days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the decree of רבי that step 24 began.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two days of blood requires six more days plus those two. Three days of blood requires seven clean days.

steps.title: Jewish women's stringency: even a mustard-seed drop needs seven clean days
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא reports that Jewish women took on themselves to count שבעה נקיים for even the smallest drop of blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: Jewish women were strict with themselves. Even if they see a drop of blood as small as a mustard seed, they sit seven clean days for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related statement. רבי זירא says Jewish women took on a very strict practice about any blood at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, some kinds of bleeding need only seven days in total, or just one clean day. The women decided to treat every sighting of blood, however small, like a זבה גדולה, who must count seven fully clean days. This makes רבי's detailed counting simpler, because one strict rule now covers every case.

keyTerms.meaning: They were strict with themselves; they took on a stringency the law did not require
A drop of blood the size of a mustard seed, meaning the smallest amount

steps.whyThisMatters: This stringency is the basis of today's practice. Any blood that makes a woman a נדה requires שבעה נקיים before טבילה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
Jewish women were strict with themselves,
so that even if they see a drop of blood the size of a mustard seed,
they sit seven clean days for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: בְּנוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל הֶחֱמִירוּ עַל עַצְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related stringency that goes beyond רבי's decree and applies one rule to every case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any blood, even a mustard-seed drop, requires seven clean days.

steps.title: Labor pains for two days, then a miscarriage on the third
steps.stepSummary: רבא has רב שמואל teach publicly that a woman who had labor pains for two days and miscarried on the third must count שבעה נקיים. The reasons: the labor-pain leniency does not apply to miscarriages, and the womb cannot open without blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא appointed רב שמואל to speak, and he taught: if she had labor pains for two days and miscarried on the third, she sits seven clean days. רבא holds that labor pains do not help for miscarriages, and that the womb cannot open without blood.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new ruling through רב שמואל about a miscarriage that came after two days of labor. Then the גמרא explains the two ideas behind the ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, blood that comes with labor pains just before a birth does not make a woman a זבה. רבא holds that this leniency does not apply to a miscarriage, so the blood of the two labor days counts. The third day also has blood, because the womb cannot open without it, even if she did not notice. That makes three days of blood, so she is a זבה גדולה and needs seven clean days.

keyTerms.meaning: He appointed him as speaker; רבא authorized רב שמואל to teach publicly
She had labor pains, a hard labor
The labor-pain leniency does not apply to miscarriages

steps.confusionAlert: The seven clean days do not come from the miscarriage alone. They come from counting three days of blood: the two days of labor plus the day of the miscarriage.

phrases.english: Rava appointed Rav Shmuel as speaker, and he taught:
phrases.notes: רבא gave the ruling, and רב שמואל announced it to the public for him.

phrases.english: If she had labor pains for two days,
and on the third day she miscarried,
she sits seven clean days.
He holds: labor pains do not count for miscarriages,
phrases.notes: He means the usual rule that blood during labor is pure does not apply when the labor ends in a miscarriage.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִפְתִיחַת הַקֶּבֶר בְּלֹא דָּם.
phrases.english: and it is impossible for the womb to open without blood.
phrases.notes: Literally 'the grave'; here the word means the womb.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new related case: a miscarriage after labor, judged by the rules of זבה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two days of labor pains followed by a miscarriage on the third day requires seven clean days. Labor gives no leniency for miscarriages, and the opening of the womb always brings blood.

steps.title: רב פפא: why mention two days of labor at all?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks רבא why the ruling depends on two days of labor. Because of רבי זירא's stringency, even a tiny bit of blood already requires שבעה נקיים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to רבא: Why specifically two days of labor? Even any small amount should be enough! For רבי זירא said: Jewish women were strict with themselves, so that even if they see a drop of blood the size of a mustard seed, they sit seven clean days for it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges the detail in רבא's ruling. He says the two days of labor seem unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא needed three days of blood to make her a זבה גדולה. רב פפא points out that because of רבי זירא's stringency, any blood at all already requires seven clean days. Since the miscarriage itself must bring some blood, the two labor days should not matter. The next step gives רבא's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically this case? A question asking why a ruling gives an unnecessary detail

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Rava:
Why specifically 'she had labor pains for two days'?
Even just any tiny amount should be enough!
For Rabbi Zeira said:
Jewish women were strict with themselves,
so that even if they see a drop of blood the size of a mustard seed,
they sit seven clean days for it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the detail in step 27 by using רבי זירא's statement from step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that depends on two days of labor before the miscarriage
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Because of רבי זירא's stringency, any drop of blood, such as the blood that comes when the womb opens, already requires seven clean days, so the two days of labor add nothing.

steps.title: A real prohibition is different from a custom
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers רב פפא: his ruling is a real איסור, while the women's stringency is only a מנהג that applies only where they adopted it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: I am telling you about a prohibition, and you are answering me with a custom?! Where the women were strict, they were strict. Where they were not strict, they were not strict.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers רב פפא's question from the last step. He explains why the 'two days of labor' detail in his ruling still matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא said רבי זירא's stringency already requires שבעה נקיים for any drop of blood, so the labor detail seems pointless. רבא answers that his ruling is a real איסור from the Torah. The women's stringency is only a מנהג, and a מנהג covers only what the women actually took on, such as a tiny drop of blood, not blood from labor.

keyTerms.meaning: A real prohibition, a binding law
A custom, a stringency people took on themselves

steps.whatToRemember: A custom reaches only as far as people actually took it on. A real איסור is binding on its own terms, so a law can still matter even when a custom seems to cover the same case.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבא is rejecting רבי זירא's report. He agrees the women are strict, but he holds that their custom does not reach blood from labor, while his own ruling is real law.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
I tell you about a prohibition,
and you tell me about a custom?!
Where they were strict, they were strict;
phrases.notes: 'They' means the Jewish women from רבי זירא's report.

phrases.english: where they were not strict, they were not strict.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמֵינָא לָךְ אִיסּוּרָא, וְאַתְּ אָמְרַתְּ מִנְהָגָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge in step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between Torah law and a custom
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי זירא's stringency makes the two-days-of-labor detail pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: The custom does not reach blood from labor, so רבא's ruling, a real איסור, is still needed for this case.

steps.title: A memory list for the coming teachings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a list of key words to help the learner remember the next group of teachings.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Proposed to her; natron; with hot water; to immerse; folds; on top of; a port. This is a memory aid.)
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא lists key words, and each one points to a teaching that is about to come.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word is a hook for an upcoming teaching. The first, תבעוה, points to רבא's ruling in the very next step. The other words point to teachings later in the sugya.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid, a list of key words

phrases.english: (Proposed to her; natron; with hot water;
phrases.notes: Here the round brackets just set apart the memory list. Each word is a hook for a teaching coming up.

phrases.english: to immerse; folds; on top of;
a port. This is a memory aid.)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Marks a shift to a new series of teachings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling. This is only a memory list.

steps.title: Accepting a marriage proposal requires seven clean days
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that a woman who accepts a marriage proposal must count שבעה נקיים before the wedding.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: If a woman was proposed to and she accepted, she must sit seven clean days.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new rule. A woman who agrees to marry must count שבעה נקיים before the wedding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that her excitement may have caused a small flow of blood that she did not notice. So she counts seven clean days and goes to the מקוה before the marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: They asked her to marry, a marriage proposal
Seven clean days without any blood

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice that a כלה counts שבעה נקיים before her wedding.

phrases.english: Rava says:
If they asked her to marry and she agreed,
she must sit seven clean days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first teaching from the memory list (תבעוה).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman who accepts a marriage proposal must count שבעה נקיים.

steps.title: רבינא delays his son's wedding by a week
steps.stepSummary: רבינא arranges for his son to marry רב חנינא's daughter, agrees to a Wednesday wedding, but then delays it by seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא arranged a match for his son with the family of רב חנינא. רב חנינא said to him: Does the master want to write the כתובה for the fourth day? He said: Yes. When the fourth day came, he waited until the next fourth day. He delayed seven days after that day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story. רבינא agrees to a Wednesday wedding, but when the day comes he pushes it off a full week.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story does not explain the delay yet. That sets up the next step, where רב חנינא asks why. The seven-day delay already hints at רבא's rule of שבעה נקיים.

keyTerms.meaning: He arranged a match, he made a שידוך

phrases.english: Ravina arranged a match for his son
in the house of Rav Chanina,
phrases.notes: He means his son would marry רב חנינא's daughter.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רב חנינא is asking רבינא.

phrases.english: Does the master think to write the marriage contract
for the fourth day?
phrases.notes: The fourth day of the week is Wednesday, the usual wedding day for a first-time bride.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes.
When the fourth day arrived,
he waited until another fourth day,
he delayed seven days
after that day.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אֶיעְסֹק לֵיהּ לִבְרֵיהּ בֵּי רַב חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story showing רבא's rule being applied in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבינא pushed the wedding off by seven days.

steps.title: רב חנינא asks why the wedding was delayed
steps.stepSummary: רב חנינא asks רבינא what the reason for the delay is.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What is this?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנינא asks רבינא why he pushed off the wedding. This sets up רבינא's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא had agreed to Wednesday and then waited a week. רב חנינא wants to know the reason for the change.

keyTerms.meaning: What is this? Why did you do this?

phrases.english: He said to him: What is this?
phrases.notes: רב חנינא is asking why the wedding was pushed off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the delay in step 32.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבינא pushed the wedding off a week.

steps.title: רבינא explains: רבא's rule of seven clean days
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that he followed רבא's rule that a woman who accepts a proposal must count שבעה נקיים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Does the master not hold of this ruling of רבא? For רבא said: If a woman was proposed to and she accepted, she must sit seven clean days.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא explains that he delayed the wedding because of רבא's rule from step 31.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the bride accepted the match, she had to count שבעה נקיים. Waiting an extra week gave her time for that.

keyTerms.meaning: Does the master hold this view?

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: Now רבינא answers רב חנינא.

phrases.aramaic: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר לְהָא דְּרָבָא,
phrases.english: Does the master not hold of this ruling of Rava,
as Rava said:
If they asked her to marry and she agreed,
she must sit seven clean days?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר לְהָא דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב חנינא's question by quoting רבא's rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The delay was for the bride to count שבעה נקיים, following רבא.

steps.title: Maybe רבא meant only an adult woman
steps.stepSummary: רב חנינא argues that רבא's rule may apply only to an adult woman who already sees blood, not to a young girl who does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You can say that רבא said this about an adult woman who sees blood. But about a young girl who does not see blood, did he say it?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנינא pushes back on applying רבא's rule to his daughter. He says the rule may only be about adult women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא worries that excitement caused bleeding, but that worry fits a woman who already has a period. A young girl who has never seen blood may not be covered. So רב חנינא suggests the delay was not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A young girl who has not reached adulthood
Did he say it? Meaning, he did not say it

steps.confusionAlert: רב חנינא is not arguing with רבא's rule itself. He only limits how far it reaches, to women who already see blood.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: Now רב חנינא is speaking again.

phrases.english: Say that Rava said it
about an adult woman who sees blood,
but about a young girl who does not see blood,
did he say it?
phrases.notes: This is a way of saying: he never said that.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַר דְּאָמַר רָבָא בִּגְדוֹלָה דְּקָחָזְיָא דְּמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether רבינא's reason applies to a young bride.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects applying רבא's rule to a young girl, not the rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבא's worry about unseen bleeding fits only a woman who already sees blood.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's use of רבא's rule (step 34) to delay the wedding of a young bride
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא's worry about unseen bleeding fits an adult who already sees blood. A קטנה who has never seen blood may not be included, so the delay was not needed.

steps.title: רבא's rule covers young girls too
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that רבא explicitly made no difference between a גדולה and a קטנה, since both are excited about the marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to him: רבא said it explicitly. There is no difference between an adult woman and a young girl. Why must an adult wait? Because she longs for the marriage. A young girl also longs for it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא pushes back on רב חנינא's suggestion and shows that רבא's rule does include a young girl.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חנינא thought the rule might be only for an adult who already sees blood. רבינא answers with two points. First, רבא said it in plain words. Second, the reason for the rule is the bride's excitement, which might bring on bleeding, and a young girl feels that excitement too.

keyTerms.meaning: She desires or longs for the marriage

steps.whatToRemember: The waiting of שבעה נקיים after accepting a proposal applies to a קטנה just as it does to a גדולה, because the reason (the excitement about the marriage) applies to both.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why רבינא delayed the wedding of רב חנינא's young daughter. It shows that the rule depends on the bride's excitement, not on whether she has already seen blood.

phrases.english: He said to him: Rava said explicitly:
phrases.notes: רבינא is answering רב חנינא here.

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא גְּדוֹלָה, לָא שְׁנָא קְטַנָּה.
phrases.english: It makes no difference whether she is an adult, and it makes no difference whether she is a minor.
For an adult, what is the reason?
Because she desires the marriage,
phrases.notes: The worry is that her excitement about marrying might cause her to bleed.

phrases.english: A minor also desires it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the distinction suggested in step 35 and defends רבינא's delay.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבא explicitly included a קטנה, and the reason (her excitement about the marriage) applies to her as well.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב חנינא's limitation of רבא's rule to an adult woman.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The rule is not based on her already seeing blood. It is based on her excitement, which a young girl also has.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explicit statement of the source plus the reason behind the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's rule might apply only to a גדולה who already sees blood.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא explicitly included a קטנה, because the rule is based on her excitement about the marriage, which a קטנה also has.

steps.title: רבא begins a new teaching about a woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new statement of רבא concerning a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A woman...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new teaching of רבא, and it is setting up a ruling that continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a fresh topic, not part of the wedding story. So far only the opening words appear: רבא is about to give a rule about a woman, and the details follow next.

phrases.english: Rava said: A woman

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the story of רבינא and רב חנינא is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A new ruling of רבא about a woman begins. Its content continues in the following text.
